independentReview.scope: Read-only lifecycle review found no correctness blocker. Three stale integration-version assertions were repaired before the frozen matrix. No reviewer execution.

scope: V9 records observer-free context creation with a null claim before asynchronous storage preparation or native allocation. If an artifact observer appears before publication, a synchronous notification reports availability without inventing a later attempt claim.

A retiring v9 observer ignores unclaimed publication. Absent observers preserve ordinary publication. Existing observed generations and earlier observer versions retain their strict admission and cleanup behavior.

Deduplication and enrollment ownership are published before the callback. Recursion guards remain active. Notification failures belong to observer disposal and cannot replace the public context creation result. Invalid native Promise returns remain owned until settlement.

Screenshot observation uses v9 and awaits both readiness and disposal. Normal creation and unclaimed notification share context bookkeeping; screenshot capture policy, pre-close behavior and output remain unchanged.
The ordinary observer-free path introduces neither a creation-claim object nor another asynchronous stage.
verification: An actual pinned runner differential starts newContext during worker module loading, holds its storage read, then resumes it after screenshot setup. Before repair, the candidate screenshot-on project fails with a runner-scope TargetClosedError while the reference and screenshot-off project pass. After repair, both projects pass for both engines.

Each runtime passes 34 controlled lifecycle groups, including eight new unclaimed-publication cases for delayed native/storage replies, retirement, generation isolation, deduplication, recursive callbacks, exact failure retention and invalid async notification custody.
Screenshot policy and cleanup units, trace archive/journal/assembly units, native runner fixtures, actual finalizer cases and packed private integration checks pass on Bun and Node 22/24.

Thirty screenshot cases per engine preserve status, retry, attachment names, dimensions and exact PNG bytes on Bun with headless shell and full Chrome, and Node 22/24 with headless shell. The two new cases retain the pending module-load race in the ordinary fixture corpus.

Bun additionally passes packed finalizer, packed runner, manual tracing and trace-off checks. Every frozen source, compiled artifact, driver and browser identity remains unchanged during the matrix. All observed watchdog processes retire cleanly; retained ZIPs pass CRC validation.

Affected provenance was regenerated and checked in the frozen verification view, then regenerated and checked against the committed API parent plus the exact verified runner diff. The second provenance view includes accepted peer code, without absorbing newer uncommitted peer changes.
reproduce: Build packages and run tools/typecheck.mjs with the pinned Bun runtime.

Run tools/test-runner-artifact-lifecycle.mjs, tools/test-runner-screenshots.mjs, tools/test-runner-trace-archives.mjs, tools/test-runner-trace-journal.mjs and tools/test-trace-archive-assembly.mjs on Bun and Node 22/24.

Run tools/test-packed-runner-integration.mjs, tools/run-runner-trace-finalizer-tests.mjs, tools/run-native-runner-tests.mjs and tools/run-runner-screenshot-tests.mjs on those runtimes; repeat the screenshot matrix with full Chrome on Bun.

Run Bun packed finalizer with --packed, tools/test-packed-runner.mjs, tools/run-manual-trace-tests.mjs and tools/run-runner-trace-off-tests.mjs. Use explicit verified browser/driver paths and external watchdogs.
limitations: This focused verification uses the accepted pre-API native driver and an isolated source view based on the preceding owned-runner commit. It does not verify the combined API/runner build or rerun Rust, full-core, Linux or package-manager layout suites.

The new lifecycle boundary preserves optional screenshot behavior but does not implement automatic trace coordination, shared per-attempt capture admission, source/action ownership across chunks or attached API capture.
Automatic runner trace policies remain unsupported. No performance, release, publication or fastest-framework claim is made.
